- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overshoots occur after recent price spikes, particularly in the first 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates when prices are falling and underestimates when rising, especially in the middle of the forecast.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs in the forecast, especially in the first 5 days.
- When true prices show strong upward momentum, model forecasts are too conservative and fail to capture the full magnitude of the move.
- Model underestimates the persistence of price trends, especially in the final 5–7 days of the forecast, where true prices often continue to trend in the direction of the recent move.
